observed_flow.note: The pre-fix analyzer used WAITING for an inbound reply request. Python Guard correctly failed closed and the user created the Task. A direction-intent semantic retry guard was then added.

Company LLM selected DATE_REPLY with self-reported confidence 0.95. A user-supplied date was inserted into the draft, the allowlisted recipient and source thread were locked, and user-approved Gmail send changed the Task to WAITING_REPLY.
The same Gmail thread was matched deterministically. A due-date shortening from 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-15 was blocked until explicit user approval.
Requested information arrived in the same thread and the Task moved from WAITING_REPLY to IN_PROGRESS.
Completion intent had self-reported confidence 0.95 but still required user approval. The final Task status became COMPLETED.

post_fix_live_semantic_check.input_kind: new scheduling reply request equivalent to the Gmail root mail

limits: The first Gmail root mail was processed before the direction-intent retry fix and therefore required user review; automatic CREATE_TASK after the fix was verified with an equivalent isolated company-LLM input, not by sending a second root Gmail mail.
This evidence proves the scoped synthetic Gmail workflow on the current local environment; it does not prove production Outlook deployment or error-free behavior for every possible mail.
LLM confidence is self-reported and is not an accuracy probability.
